mark: Marks are label plates cut like label tape: 2 px corners, mono capitals, a raised moulding with its lit top edge. A pattern mark is a tiny amber screen: dark glass with scanlines and the pattern lit in the name's own colour. The corner glyph is a lamp, the current mark is a key sunk in its well with a ring round it, and a loading mark is a small glass whose lamp lights and goes out. Look for the raised plates, the glass patterns and the dotted lamp in the corner.
stackbar: The share bar is a lit window. The free rest is a row of unlit LED cells in a dark window set in a bezel, each part is a run of lit lenses with a bright top, and the seams between parts are dark vent slots. The legend swatches are small round lamps, the title is label tape and the figures are in mono. Pointing at a part lights its rim in the LED orange. Failed reads sound the klaxon: a 3 px red frame round the note.
bullets: Each row keeps the console's LED bargraph as its bar, with the threshold as the lit tick. The figure is a Michroma count; a figure past its limit sits on a framed label tape, never a soft badge. A row that leads somewhere rises like a key under the pointer (raised, lit rim) and sinks into its well when pressed. Nothing due and failed are the empty state's plate at the list's full size with a normal Retry.
tick: A changed count prints itself in 8 frames of the ship's clock (640 ms), so the digits step in visible frames instead of gliding; digits keep their width. The tile is the case's own key-figure plate with its lamp and label tape.
uptime: The strip is a lit LED window: a dark window in a bezel, every period a lit lens (green up, amber degraded, red down) with a bright top and a faint glow; no data is an unlit outlined cell. The pointed cell is rimmed in the LED orange and grows at once, in two frames. The title is label tape, the share is Michroma, the dates are mono capitals. The quick info is the case's own popover, struck on like a tube.
uptime-states: Loading is the lamp bank computing along the whole window (five unordered patterns every 4 frames) with the shared busy card in the middle; empty and failed keep the strip's full height; a failed summary is a label-tape plate in the destructive ink.
uptime-phone: At phone width the strip keeps its window and bezel, the title never runs into the share, and the scrolling variant fades its far end; the busy card fits in its frame.
inbox: A log of rows divided by dotted vent seams. The state is a bar along the start edge (ink for new, the info ink for in flight); a row that warns or fails is framed all round in 3 px of its tone like the bridge alarm. Buttons are the console's keys with their lamps; the pressed one shows the tape reel while its row is busy. The next-up row is sunk in its well.
backlog: The same log with the job's payload folded away: opened, the payload is the ship's printout on a small amber screen (cream mono on dark glass with scanlines). Group headings are label tape with a dotted seam under them; the pressed row button shows the reel and keeps its width.
files: File rows keep the log's grammar: the file's format on label tape in the lead, titles in the body face, dotted vent seams between rows, keys with lamps for View and Open. A missing file sounds the klaxon along its row.
appointments: Appointments read as a log of days: the day is mono capitals over the hour, the next one is sunk in its well with a bar along its start edge, past ones are quieter by ink only. Group headings are label tape with a vent seam; the focus ring is the two-channel ring.
checks: Check rows are raised mouldings with a round lamp mark. A warning is framed all round in 3 px of the warning ink, a failure in 3 px of red, the same klaxon. The fix written out is a readout: cream mono under a prompt on a small dark screen with scanlines. A loading row carries the lamp bank computing along its foot.
sort: The sorted header lights its lamp: every sortable header keeps an unlit lamp before its name, so nothing shifts when a column becomes the sorted one, and the sorted one's lamp is the LED, lit, with the direction arrow after the name. A column that cannot be sorted has no lamp and no arrow. Pressing a header lights its lamp fully.
kv: Labels are label tape (mono capitals, tracked); values stay in the body or mono face. Rows with lines are divided by dotted vent seams. A changed value lights a small lamp after its label; a row that could not be read has a 3 px bar in the gap. Waiting values are the screen's glass, with its lines written in turn.
formrows: Labels are label tape; the keys under them stay mono. Rows are divided by dotted vent seams, a changed row has a 3 px bar of ink in its gap, a failed row a 3 px red bar. At phone width the aside moves under the control so a wide label never runs into it. The switch has its lamp, the fields are wells.
tiles: Each choice is a moulded key: raised at rest, a lit rim under the hand, sunk in its well while pressed and when ticked, with the title in label tape. The disabled tile is flat with a dashed edge; an invalid group is framed in red; the focus ring is the two-channel ring.
card-states: The card is a plate with its bay: loading is the busy card with the tape reel and the amber screen along its foot; empty is the empty state's well with its tape title; failed is the red alert with a normal Try again. All four fill the same bay, so the header and footer never move.
header: The mark is a label plate before the title, the title is Michroma, the badge is label tape, and the freshness line is mono capitals that tick without moving anything. The header's keys keep their lamps and press into a well.
art: Six drawings written on an amber screen: an empty cassette bay (none), a scope with no blip (nomatch), tape spilled in red off its reel (error), a jack and its socket drawn apart (offline), five lit lamps and a check (done), a key switch (locked). The screen is struck on from the top in four frames, then every vector is written in a frame apart, in whole 80 ms frames.
pipeline: The board is a rack: lanes are moulded plates, each head is label tape with the stage's colour as a lit strip, and the count is Michroma. A card is a key with its lamp in the corner (unlit, lit under the hand, full when pressed); the open card is sunk in its well with the LED lit. Marks are tape plates.
pipeline-states: Loading lays the busy card over the board with ghost cards as small glasses; empty and failed put a plate above the lanes and the lanes keep their place; a failed board is framed in 3 px of red like the alarm.
journey: The journey is the LED bargraph laid between the steps: the way travelled is lit cells in the step's colour, the way to come is unlit cells, a failed way alternates red cells. Steps are keys; the step it stands at is sunk in its well with its lamp lit in its colour. Names are label tape, dates mono. The dated line under it uses lamps for moments.
journey-states: Loading is the lamp bank with the busy card; empty and failed keep the path's full footprint, the failed one with a normal Retry and the klaxon frame.
contact: Moments are lamps on the timeline (shape and colour keep the kind), planned ones are unlit; two marks on a day are a label-tape count; the wait since the last contact and the holiday band are runs of lit cells; pointing at a mark lights a ring round it in the LED.
contact-states: Loading is the busy card over the plot with ghost lanes as glass; empty and failed fill the plot's footprint with their sentence on the plate; nothing under them moves.
secret: The value is a screen: cream mono on dark glass in the bezel. Shown, it is written by the raster, top down, in 8 frames. The countdown is an LED bargraph that goes out cell by cell. A failed read is label tape framed in 3 px of red; not yours to read is a flat dashed well.
secret-phone: At phone width the value, Reveal and Copy wrap onto lines of their own and the line under them keeps its room; the wrapped value keeps four lines of room.
manage: The wide dialog is struck on like a tube; its sections are divided by dotted vent seams with label-tape headings, and the danger section is framed all round in 3 px of red like the alarm. The token is a screen, the requests table keeps its mono capitals.
confirm: The confirmation lists what still uses the thing as a printout on a small amber screen; a blocked removal says so and shows no field. Its keys keep their lamps; Delete is the red key.
type-dialog: The typed confirmation lists what will be lost in a plate framed in 3 px of red; the name to type is a tape plate (dark, light letters) and the field is a mono well. The match line says Matched on the success tape, and the Delete key stays off until it matches.
type-own: The same block inside a page's own dialog: the same framed loss plate, tape name and mono field, no behaviour of its own.
type-phone: At phone width the loss plate and the field take the full width; the status line keeps one line of room so nothing moves while typing.
disc: The timer disc is a round screen: dark glass in a moulded bezel with scanlines, the time left a lit amber sector with a glow, twelve cream marks on the rim and the LED lens as the hub. The name is label tape; Start and Reset are the console's keys.
disc-states: Paused dims the sector; ended frames the face in 3 px of red and the line says Time is up on red tape; nothing flashes or breathes. The disc keeps its size in every state.
disc-phone: At phone width the disc scales to 70 % of the window at most and the name and keys stay centred under it.
countdown: The digits are amber phosphor in mono on a dark screen in the bezel, with scanlines; every digit keeps its cell, so the time never moves the layout. The name is label tape, the keys are the console's own.
countdown-states: Paused dims the digits to the quiet cream; ended frames the card in 3 px of red and the status is red tape; +1 min restarts it. Nothing flashes.
range: The presets are the console's segmented keys; the custom window in force is a key sunk in its well. The line that names the window is mono capitals; the panel is the case's popover struck on from its trigger.
range-states: A refused window sounds the klaxon on the field (a 3 px red inset) with its sentence under it; the panel keeps its height so Apply never moves.
wheel: A dial on the case: segments in the chart colours with dark ridges between them, a moulded bezel round the rim and the hub, the Spin key in the middle with its lamp. It turns in whole 80 ms frames, 45 of them on the register's decelerating curve, so it ticks like a 1979 display. The pick is written on a screen in amber mono.
cook: The step count is Michroma, the screen lamp is a real lamp (lit LED while the screen stays on), the ingredients are a printout on an amber screen with the amounts in phosphor, the note is the warning plate, Back and Next are big keys with lamps.
timers: A timer is a plate with its time on an amber screen in mono; the name and state are label tape; the bar is the LED bargraph. A finished timer is framed in 3 px of red with the name in the screen's place and a red state tape; it never flashes.
quantity: Minus and plus are the console's keys; the figure is Michroma in a well with the unit as label tape; focus is the two-channel ring, a refused word frames the well in 3 px of red; the disabled one is flat.
checklist: The shopping log: rows divided by dotted vent seams, group headings are label tape with a Michroma count, the bar's line is mono capitals, a row lights under the pointer and sinks when pressed. A ticked row is struck through; a failed list is framed in 3 px of red.
tri: Each chip is a switch with its lamp: either way is an unlit lamp, in is the key sunk in its well with the LED lit, out is the key with a 2 px red klaxon frame, a red lamp and a struck label. The summary line is mono capitals; the chip never changes width.
code: A block of code is a screen: cream mono on dark glass with scanlines in the plate's bezel, JSON keys in amber phosphor, line numbers dim. The head is label tape on the case with the console's keys; a failed block is framed in 3 px of red.
command: The command is typed on a screen: the terminal's name is label tape, the prompt is amber phosphor, the command cream mono on glass, Copy is the console's key that says Copied in the same width; where it runs is mono capitals under the bezel.
command-long: A long command wraps under its own first character after the prompt, or scrolls inside the glass with its edge faded, and the head never moves.
command-phone: At phone width the head keeps one line, the screen takes the full width and long lines wrap under the prompt.
compare: The divider is a 3 px dark rail and the handle a moulded knob with a lamp on it; pressed, it sinks in its well. Before and After are label tape; the frame is the case's raised plate with the key corner.
compare-live: Loading is the busy card with the tape reel over a quiet plate; a failed image is a plate framed in 3 px of red with its sentence and a normal Retry over the visible pane; the glide to a press runs in whole frames.
